summary: Backend-only testing for biogenic scope3 filtering based on org enabled_access. Verified GET /api/emissions and GET /api/dashboard/stats correctly hide biogenic records with biogenic_scope_selection='scope3' for orgs without 'scope1_2_3' access, while still showing them for orgs with that access. 5/5 pytest cases passed.
critical_code_review_comments: Data hygiene: 9 biogenic emission_records in DB have organization_id=null and 15 belong to org_id 'c782bc3e-3c95-493b-baaa-b900f85fe01f' (does not match OILES or Test_GHG_Somil_V1). These records are tied to facilities only and may bypass scoped queries if accessed via super_admin or facility-only paths. Recommend a data backfill to ensure organization_id is set on all emission_records for consistent access control.

In modules/emissions/router.py get_emission_records: the filter correctly compares 'scope1_2_3' in enabled_access. However, the same check is duplicated in modules/dashboards/router.py and modules/sinks/router.py - consider extracting `has_scope3_access(org)` helper in shared/auth to avoid drift.

DashboardStats.recent_records correctly excludes biogenic scope3 when access restricted (verified). However the biogenic_indirect field also drops to 0 as expected. Confirm front-end gauges (biogenic indirect tile) handle 0 gracefully.
